title: Gamma rays through lead
caption: With μ = 0.77 cm⁻¹ the transmitted fraction is I/I₀ = e^{−μx}. After 3 cm it is e^{−2.31} = 0.10: about 10% gets through. Every 0.90 cm (the half-value thickness ln 2/μ) halves the beam, in line with the lesson's ~9 mm for 1 MeV.
alt: Graph of transmitted fraction against thickness of lead from 0 to 6 cm: an exponential fall passing 0.5 at 0.90 cm and 0.10 at 3 cm.
description: The horizontal axis is the thickness of lead in centimetres; the vertical axis is the fraction of the beam transmitted.
The curve is e^{−0.77x}, from I = I₀e^{−μx} with μ = 0.77 cm⁻¹.
It reaches 0.5 at x = ln 2/μ = 0.90 cm.
At 3 cm the exponent is 2.31 and the fraction is 0.10, about 10%.
